purpose: Human ground truth for evaluating watermark/text/logo QA. Supersedes nothing: g004_watermark_human_labels_v1 (4 classes, 20 rows, all PENDING) stays readable; this adds the distinctions B3 needs.

NO_TEXT.definition: No visible text, lettering or logo anywhere in the image.

BENIGN_GARMENT_TEXT.definition: Text printed on clothing or accessories worn by the subject, integrated with fabric folds and lighting.

BENIGN_BACKGROUND_SIGN.definition: Scene signage (shop sign, poster, street sign) that belongs to the photographed environment.

BENIGN_BRAND_TEXT.definition: A brand name rendered as part of a real object in the scene (e.g. on a shirt), not composited over the image.

REAL_OVERLAY_TEXT.definition: Text composited over the image, independent of scene geometry and lighting.

REAL_OVERLAY_WATERMARK.definition: A stock/provider/creator watermark composited over the image, often repeated, translucent, or at an edge/corner.

REAL_LOGO.definition: A third-party graphical logo composited over the image, with or without text.

GENERATIVE_TEXT_ARTIFACT.definition: Pseudo-text the generator invented: letter-like shapes that do not read as a real word.

OCR_HALLUCINATION.definition: The OCR reported text where a human sees none.

UNCERTAIN.definition: The labeler cannot decide. Excluded from primary metrics, reported separately.

labelerSees: optionally the source image, to judge sameVisibleMarkInSource
blinding.rationale: A label derived from the policy's own output measures agreement with the policy, not correctness.

forbidden: production user images repurposed without consent covering this purpose
copying production images to a new store
extending retention of production media for labeling

candidateLevel: overlay recall (realPositiveClasses caught as review or reject)
benign text flag rate by class
metrics.acceptance: A policy change is not accepted on candidate metrics alone. Lower benign FPR with higher real-overlay FNR is not accepted automatically; higher recall that worsens zero-preview jobs is not accepted automatically. B1 (2026-08) looked better per candidate and moved zero-preview jobs from 1/5 to 4/5.
